newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 18.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.
* Stocks tumbled Friday amid a falling dollar and early sliding bond prices, as the Dow Industrials lost 247.37 to 7694.66.
* United Parcel Service and its Teamsters union said they are making progress in talks to resolve the union's strike.
* Cornerstone Properties agreed to buy 11 properties in six U.S. cities from a Dutch pension fund for $1.06 billion in cash and stock.
* Gillette told analysts to lower their expectations for the company's 1997 and 1998 earnings.
* CalEnergy dropped its $1.92 billion hostile bid for New York State Electric.
* British Airways and AMR's American Air Lines are preparing for the prospect of a scaled-down alliance amid regulatory resistance.
* Hong Kong's dollar may be the next target of speculators in the Southeast Asia currency crisis.
* China's central government took direct control of the country's two stock exchanges.
* IBM is launching a $90 million ad campaign for a corporate workhorse computer, the AS/400.
* Ford plans a new 'sporty' luxury sedan in 1999 for its Lincoln unit.
* Netscape will introduce a stand-alone version of its popular internet software.
* Japan's merchandise trade surplus rose by more than two-thirds in July.
* Dart Group reached a $41 million settlement with three members of its founding Haft family.
* Few investors believe Friday's stock market drop could signal the broad market decline that bears have forecast for more than a year.
